chunks: I said: A man married a woman, and when it was the wedding night, the woman went to a man who was a friend of hers and brought him into the bridal chamber. Then when the husband entered to have intercourse with his wife, the friend sprang up and the two fought in the house. The husband killed the friend, and then the woman rose and struck the husband a blow and killed him for the sake of the friend.
He said: "The woman is liable for the blood-money of the friend, and she is to be killed in retaliation for the husband."

key_terms.تَضْمَنُ: is held liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.تُقْتَلُ: she is to be killed in legal retaliation
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money, financial compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ ٱلْبِنَاءِ: the wedding night or consummation night
key_terms.يُبَاضِعُ: to have sexual intercourse with one's wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman causes a friend to be present in the bridal chamber and then kills her husband after the husband kills that friend?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling regarding liability and retaliation in a case involving unlawful intrusion, fighting, and killing on the wedding night. The ruling assigns the blood-money of the friend to the woman and establishes retaliatory execution for her killing of the husband.
